question.prompt: A building model is made at a scale of \(1:100\) relative to the actual building. If the model's volume is \(0.02\text{ m}^3\), what is the actual building's volume in \(\text{m}^3\)?

solutions.explanation: The ratio of lengths is \(1:100\), so the ratio of volumes is \(1:100^3=1:1000000\). Actual volume \(=0.02\times1000000=20000\text{ m}^3\).
solutions.title: Cube the length scale factor
